cell.n: 164: the even-index half of hard328, problems 0, 2, 4, ..., 326 (--shard 0/2)
cell.sampling: T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 / min-p 0; seed 33000000 + problem index (new seeds, not the stored 3000000 rows)
cell.grader: v3, plurality vote over the 8 samples (capped samples cast no vote), equal answers grouped with rln4_lib.agree, ties to the lowest sample

cells.command: uv run tools/gpu.py submit l40s --hours 2 -- "bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model base --prompt cue --set hard328 --shard 0/2 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 33000000 --samples 8 --restarts 0 --max-tokens 2048 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)" && uv run --no-project --with numpy --with math-verify==0.9.0 python -m studies.rlneurons.analysis.day1_vote --run runs/<job> --out studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_cap2k_s8-01
cells.readout: right answers (grader v3) of the plurality vote over 8 samples on the 164 problems
cells.why: f2-m01 says hard328 solutions need 6,000-14,000 tokens, so 2,048-token samples reach only the problems with short solutions. One stored base sample has about 50 of 328 right within 2k and 81 within 4k (result-1b6bf2), and a vote can only collect those: about 42 of 164. stopping-m01 says a longer cap turns abstentions into mostly wrong late answers, so a vote gains far less from more cap than one sample does. From cap 2k to 16k one sample gains about 55 on this half (about 25 to 80.5); the 16k vote is about 100 (192/328 at 4 samples, result-5c961a). If the vote gains at most half of the single's 55, it must already be about 72 or more at 2k.

best_base.note: No base-only cell has 8 samples on hard328, and no count exists for this half. Best base-only count on hard328: 199/328, vote over 4 after restarts (up to 12 generations per problem) with ties to the shortest. Scaled to the 164 even-index problems: 99.5. The plain 4-sample vote, 192/328 (result-5c961a), scales to 96.

cell.model: Think-SFT + 2 x (RL-Math 3.1 - base): delta_sum --host think_sft --donor rl_math --alpha 2 (all tensors, bf16), written to /tmp/theta
cell.prompt: cue (base cue on the raw template, as in the stored Think-SFT cue cells)
cell.set: fresh2026 (136 competition problems published in 2026: AIME, HMMT Feb and Nov)
cell.sampling: T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 / min-p 0; seed 71000000 + problem index

cells.command: uv run tools/gpu.py submit l40s --hours 2 -- "bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && rm -rf /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.delta_sum --host think_sft --donor rl_math --alpha 2 --dir /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_fresh --model-path /tmp/theta --model-label tsft_plus2rl --prompt cue --set fresh2026 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 71000000 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
cells.readout: right answers with grader v3 of 136 (metrics.json right_v3); cap hits and right/finished reported beside it
cells.why: On fresh2026 Think-SFT caps 45.6 % of samples (about 62 of 136) and gets 59.5 of its 74 finished answers right (result-5251c9). The 2x RL delta cuts cap hits to about 0.57 of Think-SFT's (94.5 to 54 on hard328, result-3387ce), which converts about 27 cut answers. f2-m04 says those become mostly wrong, scattered answers: at about 30 % right the single sample rises only to about 67. stopping-m02 says cut work becomes finished answers at the host's long-problem precision (about 70 % for Think-SFT), which gives about 59.5 + 19, i.e. about 79.
